config.title: Auth Context

intro.title: Auth Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple authentication context to manage user login state across your Vue application. You'll learn how to use Vue's reactive system to create shared state that multiple components can access. The main technologies involved are Vue's reactive ref for state management and provide/inject for passing data through the component tree. By the end, you'll understand how to create a centralized auth store that tracks whether a user is logged in and make that information available to different parts of your app without prop drilling.
intro.usecase: Auth Context is a fundamental pattern for managing user authentication state across an entire Vue application, similar to how a dashboard or admin panel needs to know if a user is logged in to display personalized content or restrict access. For example, in an e-commerce site, the shopping cart icon, user profile menu, and checkout page all need immediate access to the current user's login status and details without prop-drilling through every component. This pattern is essential for building secure, maintainable applications where authentication state must be consistently available, such as in banking apps that show account balances only after login or SaaS platforms that conditionally render features based on user roles.

objectives: Construct a reactive authentication state using Vue's Composition API
Initialize and configure a centralized auth store with user data and tokens
Implement authentication methods for login, logout, and token validation
Bind auth state to components using provide/inject patterns
Control component rendering based on authentication status
Integrate auth context with protected routes and API calls
Manipulate auth state in response to user interactions
Update UI elements dynamically when auth state changes

steps.title: Create AuthProvider component with reactive state
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthProvider that returns a template with a single root element (like a div). The component should accept a children prop and render it inside the root element.
steps.hint: In Vue, functional components can be created using either a function declaration or an arrow function. Remember to include a return statement with JSX or a template.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic AuthProvider component that can wrap child content.
successCriteria: AuthProvider component is defined as a function that accepts children and returns a template with a single root element containing the children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your AuthProvider component accepts children and returns a template with a single root element containing those children.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthProvider component isn't properly defined. It should be a function that returns JSX/template with children rendered inside a root element.

steps.title: Initialize reactive auth state in AuthProvider
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthProvider component, create a reactive object called 'authState' that contains 'user' (set to null) and 'isAuthenticated' (set to false).
steps.hint: Use Vue's reactive() function to make the object reactive. The object should have two properties with initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component will have a reactive 'authState' object ready to track authentication data.
successCriteria: A reactive object named 'authState' is created with 'user: null' and 'isAuthenticated: false' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using reactive() and your object has both 'user' and 'isAuthenticated' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a reactive object with the two required properties inside the AuthProvider's setup function.

steps.title: Create login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthProvider component's setup function, create a function named login that updates the auth state's isAuthenticated to true and sets the user property to an object with a name property.
steps.hint: Define a function that modifies the reactive auth state you initialized earlier. Remember to use the state variable you created.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a login function inside the AuthProvider component that can update the authentication state.
successCriteria: The AuthProvider component contains a login function that sets isAuthenticated to true and assigns a user object with a name property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it properly updates both isAuthenticated and user properties in the auth state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login function is missing or doesn't correctly update the auth state. Review how to modify reactive state in Vue.

steps.instruction: Create the main App component that will use the AuthProvider. The component should be a named constant and return a template with a root div.
steps.hint: Define a constant named App with a setup function that returns a template. The template should contain a root div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined with a setup function that returns a template containing a root div.
successCriteria: App component is created as a constant with a setup function that returns a template containing a root div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the App component has a setup function that returns a template with a root div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component structure isn't quite right. Create a constant named App with a setup function that returns a template containing a root div.

steps.title: Wrap app content with AuthProvider
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, wrap the existing content with the AuthProvider component.
steps.hint: Use the AuthProvider component as a wrapper element around your app's content in the template.
